ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Transistor geometries in a CMOS inverter have been adjusted to meet the requirement for worst-case charge and discharge times for driving a load capacitor \( C \). This design is to be converted to that of a NOR circuit in the same technology, so that its worst-case charge and discharge times while driving the same capacitor are similar. The channel lengths of all transistors are to be kept unchanged. Which one of the following statements is correct?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: Widths of PMOS transistors should be doubled, while widths of NMOS transistors should not be changed.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left is a CMOS inverter, with the output terminal Out connected to the load capacitor C; the discharge path goes from Out through a single NMOS to ground. On the right is the converted two-input NOR gate, the pull-up network is series PMOS, the pull-down network is parallel NMOS, and the output terminal is likewise connected to the same load capacitor C. Reasoning: For the worst-case effective discharge of the NOR gate, possibly only one input is at high level, at which time only one parallel NMOS conducts, and capacitor C still discharges through a single NMOS. Since the process is the same, the channel length is unchanged, and the load capacitance is the same, to maintain a worst-case discharge time similar to the original inverter, the on-resistance of each NMOS in the NOR should be the same as that of the original inverter NMOS. NMOS on-resistance mainly decreases as width increases, so to maintain the same on-resistance, the width of each NMOS should remain the same as that of the inverter NMOS.

raw_record.question_text: A CMOS inverter has been sized to meet worst-case charge and discharge time requirements while driving a load capacitor C. It is to be converted into a NOR circuit in the same technology, with all channel lengths unchanged, so that the worst-case charge and discharge times for the same capacitor remain similar. How should the widths of the NMOS transistors be adjusted?

method.method_draft: Use the image to compare the pull-down paths. In the inverter, C discharges through a single NMOS. In the NOR, the NMOS devices are in parallel, so in the worst-case valid discharge only one input may be high and C still discharges through a single NMOS. Since the text says the same technology, same channel lengths, and same capacitor are used, matching the inverter discharge time requires the individual NOR NMOS on-resistance to match the inverter NMOS on-resistance. Therefore each NMOS width should remain the same, i.e. not be changed.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：左侧是一个 CMOS 反相器，输出端 Out 接负载电容 C；放电路径从 Out 经过单个 NMOS 到地。右侧是转换后的二输入 NOR 门，上拉网络为串联 PMOS，下拉网络为并联 NMOS，输出端同样接同一个负载电容 C。推理：对于 NOR 门的最坏情况有效放电，可能只有一个输入为高电平，此时只有一个并联 NMOS 导通，电容 C 仍然通过单个 NMOS 放电。由于工艺相同、沟道长度不变、负载电容相同，要保持与原反相器相似的最坏情况放电时间，每个 NOR 中 NMOS 的导通电阻应与原反相器 NMOS 相同。NMOS 导通电阻主要随宽度增大而减小，因此要保持相同导通电阻，各个 NMOS 的宽度应保持与反相器 NMOS 相同。

method.method_draft: Apply the CMOS stack-compensation rule. The inverter has one NMOS in the pull-down path. In the 2-input NOR, although there are two NMOS devices total, they are in parallel, so the pull-down worst-case series stack height is still one device. The scale factor for NMOS width is therefore 1 rather than 2. Thus the NOR NMOS transistors should use the original inverter NMOS width and should not be changed.

planner_metadata.image_role: Read from the NOR schematic that the PMOS network is stacked in series for charging, while the NMOS network is not stacked; the NMOS devices form parallel branches to ground.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Standard CMOS sizing rule: to preserve drive strength relative to an inverter, multiply the width of transistors in a series stack by the number of devices in the worst-case stack, because series resistances add. Devices that are not in series with one another do not need this stack compensation. In a NOR pull-down, the worst-case NMOS stack height is 1, so the NMOS scale factor is 1.
